newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Row between passengers forces plane diversion.
newsitem.headline: Row between passengers forces plane diversion.

text.p: An aircraft enroute from Mexico to England was diverted to Shannon airport in western Ireland early on Thursday after a drunken fracas in which a passenger was injured, officials said.
"There was some sort of conflict on board. Two men were taken off and were released by immigration authorities," sources at Shannon said.
"They were disembarked and were told to find their own way back to England," according to one official.
The Airtours Boeing 767 was flying from Cancun to Manchester.
Later police in the north-western English city said they were investigating the incident in which a middle-aged man from the city of Leeds was treated for an eye injury.
"During the flight two females and two male passengers appeared to be under the influence of drink.

"They were told about their conduct and an altercation took place between them and other passengers which resulted in the 51-year-old man suffering a blow to his eye causing a laceration," Greater Manchester Police said in a statement.
"For the safety of the plane and its passengers, the plane was diverted to Shannon airport. Inquiries are continuing."
